identity.defect: Startup never probes the connection, so an incompatible or expired server at boot surfaces only as the generic retryable restore-failure boundary

findings.dispositionReason: Downgraded from the proposed blocker: the AC's enumerated conditions are covered by the two existing state machines — first load (Connection Screen), incompatible server (probe verdict where the user acts on the URL), network interruption/recovery (restore-failure keeps the stored session, Retry re-runs the authoritative restore = refetch), session invalidation (session-expired notice + clear). Connection-class failures are never phrased as authentication failures (restore-failure copy: 'The network or the server is temporarily unavailable. Your session is still stored'), satisfying AC7's non-disguise clause. A boot-time TLS probe would add startup latency and a new pre-auth surface the spec text does not demand; recorded as a follow-up enhancement in the PR body.
evidence: authentication i18n restoreFailure copy is network-framed and session-preserving
use-authentication-runtime.ts restore path: network failures stay retryable, only server-rejected sessions clear

identity.defect: Oversized /health body destroys the request after response start without handling IncomingMessage error/aborted events, allowing a reachable target to crash Electron main instead of returning incompatible-server

findings.dispositionReason: Validated repair-introduced gap. Both standard and pinned health readers destroy ClientRequest after response start without response error/aborted handlers or a shared settle-once guard. Repair with a bounded response reader that classifies overflow as incompatible and stream failures as network-failure; cover both plain and pinned paths by real Electron E2E.

requestHealth and requestHealthOverPinnedCertificate listen only for response end; neither handles response error/aborted
